QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_50

question.text: Mr. Arjun Desai is preparing to sign off on the Annual Impact Report for Shubham Family Trust's Social Venture Fund investee NPO. The LFM shows: SMART indicators at every level, triangulated MoVs, assumptions explicitly logged with risk-register, and a documented Exit/Takeover Protocol. What is the SIA's MOST appropriate action?

answer.text: Refuse to sign citing excess documentation

Proceed to perform substantive testing per SAS-100 (evidence sampling, MoV verification, assumption-failure check), and if testing supports the reported figures, issue the assurance opinion (limited or reasonable) at the scope agreed in the engagement letter
Sign without any fieldwork since documentation is good

explanation.text: The Logic: Good documentation enables (but does not substitute for) substantive testing. Per SAS-100, the SIA must still sample evidence, verify MoVs, test assumption integrity, and only then form an opinion. A well-designed LFM makes fieldwork efficient and assurance defensible. Refusing, skipping fieldwork, or qualifying 'over-compliance' are all professionally unsound. The Trap: A and D are nonsensical responses to a well-prepared client. C fails the basic audit obligation to gather sufficient appropriate evidence regardless of paperwork quality. Cross-Exam Context: End-to-end AIR sign-off is tested in XXIII Ch 7 (SAS-100) and cross-references statutory audit opinion formation (CA curriculum) and AIF attestation (XIX-A/B/C/D/E). Assessor's Pro-Tip: A clean LFM saves fieldwork time but never replaces it. Budget enough hours to sample at least 10-15% of beneficiary claims; document your sampling approach in the engagement file; form the opinion from evidence, not paperwork.
